LESSON: NUTRITION IN ANIMALS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Life Science
Topic 1.3: Nutrition in Animals
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Nutrition in Animals, part of Life Science in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How is the human digestive system adapted to its functions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the digestion of different types of food in each region of the digestive system,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Nutrition in Animals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain the adaptations of parts of the human digestive system,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Nutrition in Animals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. perform experiments to determine presence of different nutrients in food,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Nutrition in Animals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role of different parts of the digestive system.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Nutrition in Animals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain the adaptations of parts of the human digestive system,

D. appreciate the role of different parts of the digestive system.

Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted digital devices to conduct research. Regulate screen resolution appropriately for learners who are sensitive to light,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Nutrition in Animals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: as the learner retrieves and saves information from non-print sources on the enzymes used to break down

each type of food at different regions of the digestive system and shares the information with peers using digital

presentation modes.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner uses locally available materials to make a model of the human digestive system.

Values:
● Respect: as the learner considers others’ opinion while discussing the adaptations of the human digestive system.

● Unity: as the learner works harmoniously when carrying out experiments on food tests.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. describe the digestion of different types of food in each region of the digestive system,
2. explain the adaptations of parts of the human digestive system,
3. perform experiments to determine presence of different nutrients in food,
4. appreciate the role of different parts of the digestive system.

Remember the key question: How is the human digestive system adapted to its functions?
